name: Decode and hash
summary: Decode JWT and base64, inspect UUIDs, check hashes
author: friday-core
description: Reads encoded values and checks hashes. It holds 3 tools and picks the right one from what you ask. Token decoder: Decodes a JWT (header, payload, issued and expiry times) and base64, base64url, hex, percent-encoded and \u-escaped text. A JWT is only decoded: the signature is never verified, so the result does not prove the token is genuine, and an unsigned alg none or an expired token is called out. Runs locally; the token is not stored or sent. UUID inspector: Reads one or more UUIDs from text and says what they are: nil or max, the version (random v4, name-based v3 and v5, time-based v1, v6 and v7), the variant, and for time-based versions the exact moment the identifier was made. Hash check: Computes the SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 or SHA-512 hash of pasted text (UTF-8) with the platform's own crypto and compares it with a hash someone published, naming a length mismatch (64 hex characters is SHA-256). It never reads a file; for a download it says how to hash the file in PowerShell (Get-FileHash). MD5 is not offered.
